summary.headline: Week behind target on both orders and revenue, and the year stands at 94.9% of target with the required pace well above the recent run-rate.

points.what: Orders came in at 942, or 93.6% of the weekly target, and revenue at $67,610, or 90.2% of target.
points.so_what: Both weekly targets were missed, so the week added to the year's revenue shortfall rather than reducing it.

points.what: QTD revenue is $659,577, or 97.7% of the target for the same weeks, with 3 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: With $224,509 still required against a recent weekly pace of $66,428, the quarter is set to close behind target.

points.what: Orders were up 70.3% and revenue up 67.0% on last year, against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth is real but slower than the targets were built on, which is why attainment keeps slipping.

points.what: Both orders and revenue fell week on week, rated bad, with revenue down 8.7% and orders down 2.8%.
points.so_what: The decline came from a week that was already below target, leaving no offset for the quarterly gap.

points.what: YTD revenue is 94.9% of target, and hitting the $3,888,802 full-year target requires $83,789 a week versus the current 8-week run-rate of $66,432.
points.so_what: The required pace sits far above anything achieved recently, so the full-year target is out of reach at this rate.

points.what: AOV was $84.72, down 5.8% week on week and down 3.7% on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Revenue is being carried by order counts rather than basket size, so any dip in orders hits revenue harder.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 18 May 2026 was 11.4%, up 0.5 pp week on week and 0.8 pp on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Returns are rising on both comparisons, which is a risk to the revenue that gross figures already count.

points.what: Revenue missed the weekly target by $7,380 and orders by 64, at 90.2% and 93.6% attainment.
points.so_what: The revenue miss is proportionally larger than the orders miss, so the shortfall is about value per order as much as volume.

points.what: The quarter is $15,299 behind target to date, with $224,509 needed in the remaining 3 weeks to reach the $884,086 full-quarter target.
points.so_what: Closing that gap would require weekly revenue far above the recent pace, so the quarter's position is the one to watch.

points.what: May was the only month above target at 101.2%, while Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr and June month-to-date are all behind.
points.so_what: One month ahead out of six is not enough to recover the year's cumulative gap.

points.what: EMEA orders fell 16.1% to 172, a contribution of -33 orders and 122.2% of the total weekly change.
points.so_what: EMEA alone accounts for more than the whole decline, so the drop is concentrated rather than broad-based.

points.what: Search orders fell 8.3% to 627, contributing -57 orders, or 211.1% of the total change.
points.so_what: With two-thirds of orders coming through Search, movements there set the direction for the weekly total.

points.what: APAC orders rose 5.9% to 429, contributing 24 orders and 45.5% of the week's order share.
points.so_what: The largest region grew and still could not offset the declines elsewhere.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 15.3%, up 0.3 pp week on week, though down 1.5 pp on last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth $798 of revenue, so this week's uptick works against an already missed revenue target.

points.what: New signups were 236, down 5.6% week on week and down 6.3% on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Signups are shrinking while orders grow 70.3% year on year, so the two measures are moving in opposite directions.

points.what: AOV of $84.72 sits below last year's $88.02 for the same week.
points.so_what: Order growth has to work harder to carry revenue when each order is worth less than a year ago.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 18 May 2026 reached 11.4%, its highest in the 8-week history shown.
points.so_what: Order quality is trending the wrong way alongside the fall in AOV.
